clue.text: Cost singular to get to Mars

definitions.note: a verb in the third person, 'he mars', matching the answer

parts.note: 'what's the damage?' asks what something costs, so the cost is the damage
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone working out the price of sending a single probe to the planet Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet but is the verb 'spoils'; the definition sits at the end and the cost comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or harm it, so 'mars' and 'damages' are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Fool to impersonate an army officer

parts.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
LT is lieutenant

explanation.surface: A joker dressing up as an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit or idiot is a fool.

clue.text: Maybe barista's warning, still, of criminal?

definitions.meaning: '...!' is what a coffee server might say
a still is a photograph, and a criminal's police photo is a ...

explanation.surface: Is a coffee maker's caution the giveaway to a crook?
explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of a suspect's face is a booking still, as against a moving image.

clue.text: To annoy persistently is mean!

definitions.meaning: 'what are you getting at?' asks what you mean

explanation.surface: Nagging someone is a nasty thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both nagging criticism and implying something.

clue.text: Cramming lots from university into apartments

indicators.note: into means this piece is put inside the other

parts.note: studios are one-room flats

explanation.surface: Students packing great numbers from the university into their flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies hard, cramming a lot of learning, is bookish and diligent.

clue.text: Put out leg to trap bird in port

indicators.note: to trap means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: KO, knock out, means put out cold
an owl is a bird
ON is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A footballer sticks out a leg to stop a bird at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowloon is the harbour district on the mainland side of Hong Kong, a major port.

clue.text: Runs through Kansas to catch baseball player up

indicators.note: to catch means hold the next piece inside

parts.note: KS is the US state abbreviation for Kansas

indicators.note: up, in a down answer, means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Babe Ruth was a famous baseball player

explanation.surface: A sprint across Kansas to meet a ballplayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To skewer meat is to pierce it on a rod, and kebabs is that verb as well as the dish.

clue.text: Battered cars would smoke on field

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Wrecked cars would send up smoke over a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds of smoke over a battlefield are a literal picture of the threatening signs of conflict.

clue.text: Bad mistake to have ambition

parts.note: to own something is to have it
a goal is an ambition or aim

explanation.surface: It is a serious error to be ambitious.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring against your own side is the classic self-inflicted blunder.

clue.text: Perhaps a little brandy, with food, even

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirit, brandy for one
and means with
tuck is British slang for food, especially at school

explanation.surface: A drop of brandy with a meal, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck-and-neck race is level, so the idiom means evenly matched.

clue.text: Glower, being the subject of jokes?

definitions.meaning: read as glow-er, something that glows
'how many X does it take to change a ...?' is a whole family of jokes

explanation.surface: Someone scowling because they are always being laughed at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' usually means scowl; split as glow-er it is a thing that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp's bulb gives out light, and it features in countless 'how many does it take' gags.

clue.text: Hastily make approach

definitions.meaning: to ... curtains or a dress is to make them quickly
the approach a bowler or jumper takes

explanation.surface: Throw together a way in at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means sew or build quickly; the noun is the preliminary approach or lead-in period.

clue.text: Bag and basket for lifting rubbish — everyone in favour

parts.note: hot air is empty talk, rubbish

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a boon is a favour
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A sack and a basket for hauling rubbish, with unanimous approval.
explanation.definitionFit: This aircraft is an envelope of heated gas with a passenger basket slung beneath to carry people aloft.

clue.text: Missionary's motley crew, the size reduced

indicators.note: motley means mixed and varied, so the letters are jumbled
reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A missionary's unruly crew, smaller than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts SIZE to SIZ before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Schweitzer was a medical missionary in Gabon; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Manage to expose less of that!

parts.note: to cut it is to manage or cope, as in 'can't cut it'
to out someone is to expose them

explanation.surface: A censor's demand to show less flesh in a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation tells someone to stop doing something, the same as demanding less of their behaviour.

clue.text: So-called propagandist's excessively outspoken lines about Kennedy on vacation

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters
outspoken means said out loud, so a word that sounds alike is used

parts.note: rows are lines

explanation.surface: A propagandist speaks too bluntly about Kennedy while he is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Kennedy to its outer letters; 'outspoken' asks for a word sounding like the one for lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was a nickname given by Allied troops to English-speaking Japanese radio broadcasters.

clue.text: Bright students turning away from books

indicators.note: turning means the word for students is read backwards

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
lit, short for literature, means books

explanation.surface: Clever students giving up their reading.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A place lit by the sun is bright with daylight.

clue.text: Embrace superior manner that's upset French protestant

parts.note: a hug is an embrace
U means upper class, superior

indicators.note: upset, in a down answer, means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tone is a manner

explanation.surface: A hug delivered with an air of superiority offends a French Protestant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were Calvinist Protestants of France, persecuted in the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Put up after with welcome drink

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: hi is a greeting, a welcome
to sky a ball is to hit it high, put it up

explanation.surface: Someone is given a welcome drink after arriving to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: To sky a ball, in cricket, is to hit it high into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is a classic spirit, a common drink.

clue.text: Not all, on reflection, consider us nicely covered

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Think of us kindly: not everything is protected.
explanation.definitionFit: A policyholder who is insured is covered against loss.

clue.text: Reserve's virtually shelved, being not the quickest

parts.note: a reserve is a sub, and the 's gives SUBS

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shelved plan is put on ice

explanation.surface: A substitute left on the bench is not the fastest player.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the speed of sound means slower than supersonic craft, so not the fastest.

clue.text: Drownings done, say, at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drownings carried out, you might say, out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyades were mass executions by drowning in Nantes during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Man's more than a crook maybe

definitions.meaning: to man a post is to staff it
a crook is a shepherd's staff

explanation.surface: A man is worse than a mere criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means provides workers; the plural noun means several walking sticks.

clue.text: Rare being casually dressed in court? Carry on

parts.note: wearing shorts is being casually dressed
a defendant who is up is before the court
to ply a trade is to carry it on

explanation.surface: It is unusual for someone to turn up in court in casual wear and carry on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is hard to find, which is what rare means.

clue.text: Square loaf mostly devoured by old man

indicators.note: devoured by means swallowed inside the other piece

parts.note: pa is father, the old man

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to laze is to loaf about

explanation.surface: Dad wolfs down most of a square loaf of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: Familiar form of English city rising initially behind houses

indicators.note: houses means holds the next piece inside

parts.note: bum is British slang for the behind

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter only

explanation.surface: An English city's nickname first catching on behind the houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Brum is the colloquial name for Birmingham, England's second city.

clue.text: Back-to-back golds by previously unknown Spanish hero

indicators.note: previously means this piece comes before the next

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
OR is heraldic gold; two placed back to back read OR then RO

explanation.surface: An unknown athlete winning gold medals in successive events.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked swordsman of fiction is a Spanish Californian folk hero.

clue.text: European most of the way flanked by keeper, presumably?

indicators.note: flanked by means one piece has the other on each side

parts.note: 'finders keepers' suggests a finder is a keeper

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a lane is a way

explanation.surface: A long journey with a goalkeeper on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finders keepers' is the playground rule that whoever finds something keeps it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Nordic country of Finland is a European.

clue.text: Right and left-wingers penning notes

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: reds are socialists, left-wingers
re is a note of the scale; RES is its plural

explanation.surface: Political sides, right and left, writing down memos.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to right or remedy it.

clue.text: Member that comes across price for delivery on time

indicators.note: in an across answer, A on B puts A after B

parts.note: a ransom is the price paid for a hostage's release, or delivery

explanation.surface: A courier part that arrives punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: This horizontal beam spans a window or door, a structural member lying crosswise.
